en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing across {city}
market: Every other province has a centre of gravity. {city} has three, and Moncton, Saint John and Fredericton are close enough in size that none of them is the obvious answer. That has a practical effect most owners underestimate: a campaign aimed at one of them is aimed at roughly a third of the province, and a campaign aimed at all three is genuinely a provincial campaign rather than a city one with spillover. Deciding which of those you are running is the first real decision here.

The second is language. {city} is officially bilingual, and in the north and east a large share of your customers search in French. The words they type are not translations of the English ones, so a campaign that was written in English and run through a translator buys phrases nobody uses. If part of your market is francophone, the French keyword research has to be done from scratch rather than converted.

Beyond that, this is a small and well-connected business community where reputation travels quickly and where competition for search is thin. In {industries}, publishing a genuinely useful explanation of how you work is often enough to take the top of the results, which is not something I can say about a larger province.

en.servicesIntro: Same three services everywhere I work. What changes in {city} is that you have to decide which centres and which language you are actually competing in.

services.title: Google Ads Management
services.body: In {city} that means being deliberate about which of the three centres you are buying, and running French and English as separate work rather than as a translation. Then account structure, then cutting spend on searches that were never going to convert.

services.title: SEO Consulting
services.body: Usually the better first investment here, because a province-wide organic position is achievable at this size and because {city} buyers research carefully before they call. Technical fixes first, then the pages that answer the real questions.

services.title: AIO Consulting
services.body: Being the {city} business ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews name when someone asks for a recommendation. In a province this size the named shortlist is very short, which makes this the best value of the three.

area.citiesBody: Moncton and Saint John have their own pages because they are genuinely different problems: one is a bilingual distribution hub, the other an industrial port where some growth is not a marketing question at all. There is no Fredericton page, because on the evidence I have it is not a separate market from the other two rather than a smaller version of them.
area.districtsBody: I take on clients throughout {districts}. Everything is run remotely over video and email, so where in the province you are makes no difference to the work or the price.
area.nearbyBody: I work with businesses in {nearby} on the same terms.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

If any real share of your customers is francophone, yes, and translating the English ones is not the same thing. French search terms are different words, not converted words, so the research has to be redone. I will be straight about my own limits here: I build the French campaigns, and for customer-facing copy aimed at a francophone audience I have it reviewed by a native speaker before it runs.

faq.q: Do Moncton and Saint John have their own pages?
faq.a: They do now, and only because each one turned out to need advice this page cannot give. Moncton is genuinely mixed between English and French, so a single-language campaign there leaves a large part of the market unaddressed. Saint John is an industrial port where a lot of B2B growth runs through procurement rather than search, and the honest answer for those businesses is that advertising is the wrong instrument. There is still no Fredericton page, because I have not found an argument it would carry that these two do not.

faq.q: Is the market too small for this to pay off?
faq.a: For paid search it sometimes is, and I will tell you when the volume does not justify the channel. For SEO and AI visibility the small size works in your favour, because a province-wide position is achievable here in a way it never is in Ontario.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
